title: Maximizing Construction Margins in a High-Rate Environment
summary: Elevated interest rates are testing construction margins. See how financing, project costs and market shifts could shape your next move.
body_markdown:
The construction industry creates jobs, supports economic growth, and shapes the physical infrastructure of a nation. Like every sector, it is influenced by a variety of economic factors, and interest rates are among the most significant.


More than two years after interest rates began climbing, many construction companies continue to operate in a higher-cost borrowing environment. After three rate cuts in late 2025, the benchmark federal funds rate has remained between 3.50% and 3.75% throughout 2026. As contractors, developers and project owners plan for the future, elevated interest rates continue to influence[financing decisions](https://www.cbiz.com/insights/article/effective-cash-flow-management-in-construction) , project planning and market activity.


## Five Ways Higher Rates Impact Construction


Interest rates, set by central banks, influence borrowing costs for businesses and individuals alike. When interest rates rise and lending requirements tighten, borrowing becomes more expensive, creating challenges across the construction industry.


### Financing Costs


One of the most immediate and direct impacts of rising interest rates is increased financing costs. Construction projects often require significant capital, and contractors, developers, and homeowners frequently rely on loans to fund these projects. Higher interest rates mean higher borrowing costs, which can reduce the profitability of projects, particularly for smaller construction firms.


### Reduced Investment


When interest rates are low, the construction industry tends to experience increased investment, as borrowing is more affordable. Conversely, rising interest rates can discourage investment, leading to a slowdown in construction activity. This can result in delayed or canceled projects, impacting job creation and economic growth.


### Housing Market


When benchmark rates stay elevated, mortgage rates tend to follow. According to Freddie Mac, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate has hovered near 6.7% through much of 2026 while Fannie Mae projects a 6.5% average for the year. Higher mortgage rates reduce the purchasing power of potential homebuyers, dampening demand for new residential construction and creating challenges for homebuilders.


### Project Viability


Construction projects often have long lead times and planning horizons. As interest rates rise, the cost projections for these projects may no longer align with initial estimates. This can lead to projects becoming financially unviable, potentially causing delays or cancellations.


### Commercial Real Estate


Rising interest rates also affect the commercial real estate sector. Higher borrowing costs can deter businesses from expanding or investing in new office spaces, retail locations, or industrial facilities, thereby affecting the demand for commercial construction. Remote work is also affecting demand for office space as companies seek to right-size their operations.


## How Construction Companies Can Manage Higher Rates


While rising interest rates can pose challenges for the construction industry, companies can take several steps to manage their impact:


### Efficient Project Management


To offset increased financing costs, construction companies should focus on improving project efficiency and cost management. Implementing lean construction practices can help reduce overall project expenses. Helping project owners prioritize needs versus wants through value engineering and project staging can improve funding success.


### Diversify Funding Sources


Diversifying funding sources beyond traditional bank loans can provide construction firms with more financial stability. Private equity, venture capital, and partnerships can offer alternatives to mitigate the effects of rising interest rates.


### Managing Costs


According to Associated Builders and Contractors’ analysis of Producer Price Index data, nonresidential construction input prices were up 7.4% year over year as of July 2026. Additionally, data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics shows overall construction input prices have risen more than 43% since early 2020, with tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper contributing to pricing pressures. Exploring alternative risk financing strategies may help maximize potential cost savings for insurance and employee benefits. Many firms struggle not because of a lack of work, but because of financial management challenges and operational inefficiencies.


### Seeking ROI


Construction companies cannot rely on “the way we’ve always done things.” Spending should be intentional and deliver a measurable return on investment. Investing in technology and automation can enhance productivity and reduce rising labor costs.


### Long-Term Financing


Locking in long-term financing options when interest rates are low can provide protection against future rate hikes. Fixed-rate loans offer stability in a potentially volatile financial environment.


### Market Research


Staying informed about local market conditions and adapting to changing demand patterns can help construction companies make informed decisions as interest rates change.

#### Frequently Asked Questions


Rising interest rates increase the cost of borrowing for contractors, developers, and project owners. Higher financing costs can reduce project profitability, make it more difficult to secure funding, and cause some projects to be delayed, scaled back, or put on hold until market conditions improve. As borrowing becomes more expensive, construction firms often face greater pressure to manage costs, improve efficiency, and carefully evaluate project investments.


Higher interest rates can reduce construction activity by making financing less affordable and discouraging investment. Residential construction is often affected when higher mortgage rates reduce homebuyers’ purchasing power, while commercial projects may face tighter lending conditions and increased project costs. As a result, some developers and businesses may postpone construction plans until financing conditions become more favorable.


Construction companies can adapt by focusing on financial discipline, improving project efficiency, diversifying funding sources, and making data-driven decisions about investments and operations. Evaluating project costs early, identifying inefficiencies, exploring alternative financing options, and staying informed about market conditions can help firms better manage risk and maintain long-term stability during periods of higher interest rates.
